company-fundamentals.hook: A share price tells you what people will pay today. The financials tell you what the business is actually worth doing. Learn to read both.
fun: A company can report a profit and still run out of cash: profit is an opinion, cash is a fact.
A low P/E is not automatically cheap: it can mean the market expects earnings to fall.
traps: Comparing P/E ratios across very different industries.
Ignoring debt when a company’s profit looks strong.
Reading promoter pledging as a minor detail.

i.prompt: Which statement about “Free cash flow” is correct?
options: Free cash flow is the same as net profit.
Free cash flow is cash from operations minus the money spent to maintain and grow the business. It is what is truly left for owners and lenders.
The profit and loss statement lists everything the company owns and owes on one date.
EPS is the dividend actually paid to each shareholder.
i.why: Correct: Free cash flow is cash from operations minus the money spent to maintain and grow the business. It is what is truly left for owners and lenders. The other statements are common misunderstandings.

i.prompt: Which term is described here? The balance sheet is a snapshot on one date of what a company owns (assets), what it owes (liabilities) and the owners’ stake (equity).
i.why: Balance sheet: The balance sheet is a snapshot on one date of what a company owns (assets), what it owes (liabilities) and the owners’ stake (equity).

i.prompt: Which statement about “Revenue growth” is correct?
options: Revenue growth is the rate at which a company’s sales increase over time. Steady growth over many years suggests healthy demand.
One year of high revenue growth proves a company is excellent.
EPS is the dividend actually paid to each shareholder.
A higher debt-to-equity ratio always means a stronger company.
i.why: Correct: Revenue growth is the rate at which a company’s sales increase over time. Steady growth over many years suggests healthy demand. The other statements are common misunderstandings.

i.prompt: Which term is described here? Dividend yield is the annual dividend per share divided by the share price, shown as a percentage. It is the cash return before any price change.
i.why: Dividend yield: Dividend yield is the annual dividend per share divided by the share price, shown as a percentage. It is the cash return before any price change.

i.prompt: Which term is described here? Return on equity is net profit divided by shareholders’ equity. It shows how well a company turns owners’ money into profit.
i.why: Return on equity (ROE): Return on equity is net profit divided by shareholders’ equity. It shows how well a company turns owners’ money into profit.

i.prompt: Which term is described here? Earnings per share is net profit divided by the number of shares. It shows how much profit each share earns.
i.why: Earnings per share (EPS): Earnings per share is net profit divided by the number of shares. It shows how much profit each share earns.

i.prompt: Which statement about “Interest coverage ratio” is correct?
options: Interest coverage is operating profit divided by interest expense. It shows how comfortably a company can pay its interest bills.
Interest coverage measures how much dividend a company pays.
The profit and loss statement lists everything the company owns and owes on one date.
Net profit margin can never be lower than operating margin.
i.why: Correct: Interest coverage is operating profit divided by interest expense. It shows how comfortably a company can pay its interest bills. The other statements are common misunderstandings.

i.prompt: Which term is described here? The profit and loss statement shows a company’s revenue, costs and profit over a period such as a quarter or a year.
i.why: Profit and loss statement: The profit and loss statement shows a company’s revenue, costs and profit over a period such as a quarter or a year.

i.prompt: Which term is described here? The cash flow statement shows actual cash moving in and out through operations, investing and financing.
i.why: Cash flow statement: The cash flow statement shows actual cash moving in and out through operations, investing and financing.

i.prompt: Which statement about “Operating margin” is correct?
options: Operating margin is operating profit as a percentage of revenue. It shows how much profit is left from each rupee of sales before interest and tax.
Operating margin is the same as the dividend payout.
Net profit margin can never be lower than operating margin.
A high dividend yield always means a safe company.
i.why: Correct: Operating margin is operating profit as a percentage of revenue. It shows how much profit is left from each rupee of sales before interest and tax. The other statements are common misunderstandings.

i.prompt: Which term is described here? The PEG ratio divides the P/E by the expected earnings growth rate, to judge whether a high P/E is justified by growth.
i.why: PEG ratio: The PEG ratio divides the P/E by the expected earnings growth rate, to judge whether a high P/E is justified by growth.

i.prompt: Which term is described here? The P/B ratio compares the share price with book value per share, the net worth of the company divided by shares. It is often used for banks.
i.why: Price-to-book (P/B) ratio: The P/B ratio compares the share price with book value per share, the net worth of the company divided by shares. It is often used for banks.

i.prompt: Which statement about “Net profit margin” is correct?
options: Net profit margin is net profit as a percentage of revenue. It shows how much of each rupee of sales finally becomes profit after all costs and taxes.
Net profit margin can never be lower than operating margin.
A company that reports profit always has plenty of cash.
A high dividend yield always means a safe company.
i.why: Correct: Net profit margin is net profit as a percentage of revenue. It shows how much of each rupee of sales finally becomes profit after all costs and taxes. The other statements are common misunderstandings.

i.prompt: Which statement about “Pledged shares” is correct?
options: Pledged shares are promoter shares put up as security for a loan. If the price falls, lenders can sell them, which can hit the share price.
Pledged shares are shares reserved for new investors in an IPO.
ROE shows how much debt a company has.
The balance sheet shows how much profit was earned during the year.
i.why: Correct: Pledged shares are promoter shares put up as security for a loan. If the price falls, lenders can sell them, which can hit the share price. The other statements are common misunderstandings.

i.prompt: Which statement about “EV/EBITDA” is correct?
options: EV/EBITDA is the price you pay for a single share.

EV/EBITDA compares the whole value of a business (market value plus net debt) with its operating earnings before interest, tax and depreciation. It lets you compare companies with different debt levels.
P/B compares price with sales per share.
The PEG ratio measures how much dividend a share pays.
i.why: Correct: EV/EBITDA compares the whole value of a business (market value plus net debt) with its operating earnings before interest, tax and depreciation. It lets you compare companies with different debt levels. The other statements are common misunderstandings.

i.prompt: Which statement about “Current ratio” is correct?
options: The current ratio measures long-term growth in profit.
One year of high revenue growth proves a company is excellent.
The current ratio is current assets divided by current liabilities. It shows whether a company can meet its short-term obligations.
Promoter holding is the share of profit paid to employees.
i.why: Correct: The current ratio is current assets divided by current liabilities. It shows whether a company can meet its short-term obligations. The other statements are common misunderstandings.

i.prompt: Which statement about “Promoter holding” is correct?
options: Promoter holding is the share of profit paid to employees.
Free cash flow is the same as net profit.
Promoter holding is the percentage of a company owned by its founders or controlling group. Stable, high holding shows commitment, but quality still matters.
Net profit margin can never be lower than operating margin.
i.why: Correct: Promoter holding is the percentage of a company owned by its founders or controlling group. Stable, high holding shows commitment, but quality still matters. The other statements are common misunderstandings.

i.prompt: Which term is described here? The P/E ratio is the share price divided by earnings per share. It shows how much investors pay for each rupee of earnings.
i.why: Price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio: The P/E ratio is the share price divided by earnings per share. It shows how much investors pay for each rupee of earnings.

i.prompt: Which statement about “Debt-to-equity ratio” is correct?
options: A higher debt-to-equity ratio always means a stronger company.
Promoter holding is the share of profit paid to employees.
The debt-to-equity ratio compares a company’s borrowings with owners’ equity. A higher number means more reliance on borrowed money.
Net profit margin can never be lower than operating margin.
i.why: Correct: The debt-to-equity ratio compares a company’s borrowings with owners’ equity. A higher number means more reliance on borrowed money. The other statements are common misunderstandings.

i.prompt: Which term is described here? ROCE is operating profit divided by all capital used, both equity and debt. It shows how efficiently the whole business uses money.
i.why: Return on capital employed (ROCE): ROCE is operating profit divided by all capital used, both equity and debt. It shows how efficiently the whole business uses money.

h.why: This is Dividend yield. Dividend yield is the annual dividend per share divided by the share price, shown as a percentage. It is the cash return before any price change.

h.why: This is Balance sheet. The balance sheet is a snapshot on one date of what a company owns (assets), what it owes (liabilities) and the owners’ stake (equity).
